findings.description: The check `if fg:` replaces `if fg is not None:`, so a falsy but valid color is silently skipped. Integer color 0 (black in the 256-color palette) is dropped, as is an empty-string color.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=0)` or `bg=0`. The falsy value fails the truthiness test, so no escape code is emitted. The user gets uncolored text instead of black with no error. The same defect applies to `bg` at line 684.

findings.description: `_interpret_color` no longer validates its input. Out-of-range ints (e.g. 300, -1) and bools produce invalid escape codes. Tuples of the wrong length raise an unpacking ValueError, and tuples with values outside 0-255 produce malformed codes.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg=300)` or `fg=(1, 2)`. Previously this raised ValueError('Unknown color'). Now an invalid ANSI sequence is emitted silently, or a confusing unpacking ValueError is raised. Other callers of `_interpret_color` see KeyError for bad strings.

findings.description: The exception type for an unknown color changed from ValueError to TypeError, which breaks callers that catch ValueError.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg='nocolor')`. It now raises TypeError instead of ValueError. Existing code and tests that catch ValueError will fail to handle it.
